pr_title: perf: Remove cast to boolean after comparison in optimizer
pr_body:
* Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/21009
  * The expression gets recognized by `collapse_joins` without issue after we remove the extra cast
* Fixes https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/issues/21023
  * Updates some old code to propagate `options: CastOptions` instead of `strict: bool`

Drive-by renames `fn coerce_types()` to `fn optimize_exprs()` under `ConversionOptimizer`, as it also does other optimizations aside from type coercion.

issue_context.title: Incorrect overflowing cast of literals containing Series
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
pl.LazyFrame().select(pl.lit(pl.Series([128], dtype=pl.Int64)).cast(pl.Int8, wrap_numerical=True)).collect()
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────┐
│      │
│ ---  │
│ i8   │
╞══════╡
│ null │
└──────┘
```


### Log output

```shell

```

### Issue description

Went to non-strict (replace with NULL) instead of overflowing (wrapping).


### Expected behavior

```python
shape: (1, 1)
┌──────┐
│      │
│ ---  │
│ i8   │
╞══════╡
│ -128 │
└──────┘
```

### Installed versions

1.21.0

review_comments: Do you know why this not returns `None`? I understand it returns the same `aexpr` untouched.

The `aexpr` in this function is the input expr to the cast (not the cast itself), you can see how it is called if you expand the diff above -
![Screenshot_20250201_002429_Chrome](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ca378fa-11a4-4337-a14d-52eb28ad09f7)

So by returning it here we replace the cast expr with its input, which removes the cast.
